subject: Music Production
title: The Beatles' Revolutionary Mixes
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Beatles' Revolutionary Mixes.

hook.text: The Beatles and engineer Geoff Emerick broke nearly every studio rule at Abbey Road Studios.

buildup.text: They placed microphones inside drums, compressed vocals beyond accepted limits, and played tapes backward.

discovery.text: 'Sgt. Pepper' used revolutionary techniques like ADT, vari-speed, and random tape loops in its mix.

twist.text: The entire album was mixed to mono first because stereo was considered a novelty at the time.

climax.text: The Beatles' mixes expanded what studios were capable of and inspired generations of engineers.

punchline.text: Breaking every studio rule created the most influential album.

quiz.question: Why was 'Sgt. Pepper' mixed to mono first?
options: Stereo equipment hadn't been invented yet
Stereo was considered a novelty at the time
